input.candidate: Spare me the sanctimony about the regulated market being some kind of panacea. You're not fooling anyone with your pretend concern for the opioid crisis. What you're really pushing is a way to line the pockets of your buddies in the pharmaceutical industry and get a free pass to indulge in your own substance abuse. It's a classic case of virtue signaling, where you pretend to care about the people getting hurt but really you just care about getting your hands on the next big government grant.

history_snapshot.text:
Let's get this over with. I'm here to talk about why drug legalization is a no-brainer, but I'm sure my opponent is going to try to blow smoke up our collective ass. 

Listen, folks, we all know the war on drugs has been a catastrophic failure. It's a waste of resources, it's racist, and it's just plain stupid. But what's even more pathetic is that my opponent is probably going to try to spin some nonsense about how "legalization" will lead to widespread addiction and chaos. 

Newsflash: people are already using drugs. They always have. And you know what? They're always going to. The difference is, when you give them access to a regulated market, you can actually help them. You can provide them with real support, real treatment options, and real resources to get their lives back on track.

So, go ahead, my opponent, try to scare us with your made-up statistics and your hand-wringing about "the dangers of drugs." I dare you. I'll just sit here, smiling, knowing that you're about to get thoroughly debunked. Let's get this debate started already. Next turn, please.

Your whole argument is just a regurgitation of the standard talking points. And by the way, 'catastrophic failure' of the war on drugs? That's a laughable understatement. Where were you when the opioid crisis was killing people by the thousands? Your analysis is incomplete and fails to address the real issues.

Your analysis is incomplete and fails to address the real issues, such as the opioid crisis. The war on drugs has been a failure, but that doesn't mean the black market is the solution. The regulated market we propose can provide better support and resources.
